53594}}}} | order = 14th [[United States Ambassador to the Bahamas]] }} '''Herschel Junior Walker''' (born March 3, 1962) is an American [[diplomat]] and former professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] who has served as [[List of ambassadors of the United States to the Bahamas|United States ambassador to the Bahamas]] since 2025. A member of the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]], he previously played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 12 seasons. He was the Republican nominee in the [[2022 United States Senate election in Georgia|2022 U.S. Senate election in Georgia]]. Walker played [[college football]] at the [[University of Georgia]], where he won the [[Heisman Trophy]] in 1982.{{cite web |title=1982 Heisman Trophy |url=http://heisman.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=49 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411082750/http://heisman.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=49 |archive-date=April 11, 2017 |access-date=March 11, 2017}} He spent the first three seasons of his professional career from 1983 to 1985 with the [[New Jersey Generals]] of the [[United States Football League]] (USFL) and was [[Most valuable player|MVP]] in his final year with the league. After the USFL folded, Walker joined the NFL with the [[Dallas Cowboys]], earning consecutive [[Pro Bowl]] and second-team [[All-Pro]] honors from 1987 to 1988. In 1989, [[Herschel Walker trade|Walker was traded]] to the [[Minnesota Vikings]], which is regarded as one of the most lopsided trades in NFL history and credited with establishing the Cowboys' [[Dynasty (sports)|dynasty]] of the 1990s. He was later a member of the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and [[New York Giants]] before retiring with the Cowboys. Walker was inducted to the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 1999. Outside of football, Walker was a member of the United States' [[bobsleigh]] team at the [[1992 Winter Olympics]] and pursued business ventures in food processing. From 2019 to 2020, he served as a co-chair on the [[President's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition]] under President [[Donald Trump]]. Walker launched his first political campaign in Georgia's 2022 U.S. Senate election, losing to [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Raphael Warnock]] in a runoff.{{cite news |last=Stahl |first=Chelsea |date=December 7, 2022 |title=Democratic Sen. Warnock defeats Republican Walker in Georgia runoff |language=en-US|publisher=[[NBC News]]|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2022-election/georgia-senate-runoff-election-polls-close-results-rcna60156 |access-date=December 7, 2022}} In 2025, Walker was [[Senate confirmation hearing|confirmed]] by the Senate in a 51–47 vote as the United States ambassador to the Bahamas during Trump's second presidency.{{Cite news |date=October 7, 2025 |title=Senate confirms Herschel Walker as ambassador to the Bahamas |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2025/10/07/herschel-walker-ambassador-bahamas-senate-vote/ |access-date=October 8, 2025 |work=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}{{Cite news |last=Ward |first=Jasper |last2=Ward |first2=Jasper |date=October 7, 2025 |title=Ex-NFL star Herschel Walker confirmed as first U.S. Bahamas ambassador in nearly 15 years |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/ex-nfl-star-herschel-walker-confirmed-first-us-bahamas-ambassador-nearly-15-2025-10-07/ |access-date=October 8, 2025 |work=Reuters |language=en}}

Head of football development }} '''Hines Edward Ward Jr.''' (born March 8, 1976) is an American [[American football|football]] coach and former player who is the [[wide receiver]]s coach and associate head coach for [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State]]. He played as a wide receiver in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) after being selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the third round of the [[1998 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]]. Ward played his entire professional career for the Steelers and he became the team's all-time leader in receptions, receiving yardage and touchdown receptions. Ward was voted MVP of [[Super Bowl XL]] and upon retirement was one of eleven NFL players to have at least [[List of National Football League career receptions leaders|1,000 career receptions]]. '''McCurey Hercules "Herkie" Walls''' (born July 18, 1961) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]], where he also ran [[Track and field|track]], and was selected by the [[Houston Oilers]] in the seventh round of the [[1983 NFL draft]]. He was also a member of the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].

Walls also played football for the [[Orlando Predators]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) and the [[Sacramento Surge]] of the [[World League of American Football]] (WLAF). He was selected to the [[Arena Football Hall of Fame]] in 2000. He was the head coach of the [[Orlando Predators (2019)|Orlando Predators]] of the [[National Arena League]], a separate franchise from the AFL team of the same name, in 2023. Walls was also named to the 1980 United States Olympic track and field team, but did not participate in [[1980 Summer Olympics|that year's Olympics]] due to the American [[1980 Summer Olympics boycott|boycott of the games]].
